ai_policy.summary: Journal permits generative AI assistance, including research programming and proofreading or polishing author-written text, subject to disclosure and human responsibility. Its explicit writing examples do not establish permission for substantive AI manuscript drafting.

disclosure.instructions: Disclose any use of generative AI in Comments for the Editor in the submission form.

restrictions: Authors must review accuracy, bias, integrity and completeness; cite appropriately and comply with privacy, ethics and law.

policy_sources.applicability: Journal-specific author information or applicable publisher policy as described.
policy_sources.note: Broadly permits assistance in work; explicit examples are research programming and proofreading or polishing human-written text. Substantive drafting is not explicitly established.

findings.issue: Broad generative AI assistance permits programming and polishing, but the author page explicitly names editing of human-written prose and does not explicitly establish substantive drafting. The compatible classification overstates this evidence.
findings.resolution: Set compatibility unclear and manuscript drafting not_stated; retain mandatory disclosure and responsibilities.

findings.issue: Submission-year and acceptance-year counts have different populations, and 2025 cohort was incomplete at the April 2026 snapshot.
findings.resolution: Preserved dated figures and cohort caveats; no derived acceptance rate.

notes: Inspected all 20 baseline plus discovery records and the fee, geography, and AI role patches. Independently read the official JOSS, JGAA and TheoretiCS AI policies, JAIR fee FAQ, JSS submission guide, JMLR news and TheoretiCS statistics. Other venue claims were inspected from the other role files and not independently reverified; no claim of complete independent source coverage.
Added official historical JMLR 2004 impact factor; existing reported metrics retained with date and population. Citation impact is not acceptance probability. No subjective difficulty judgments.
